title: The Collector’s Guide to Antique and Vintage Jewelry Styles
summary: Here's what to look for when shopping for authentic pieces.
body_markdown:
[Van Cleef & Arpels Art Deco Ruby, Sapphire and Diamond Brooch, 1920–29](https://www.1stdibs.com/jewelry/brooches/brooches/van-cleef-arpels-art-deco-ruby-sapphire-diamond-brooch/id-j_27364852/)


If you’re new to collecting[antique](https://www.1stdibs.com/buy/vintage-jewelry/) and[vintage jewelry](https://www.1stdibs.com/buy/vintage-jewelry/) , you might find it difficult to identify an item’s style or era. An enamel pendant or a delicate platinum ring might give clues, but different eras don’t start and stop on certain dates.


So, what are the important antique- and vintage-jewelry styles, and how can you recognize them? To start, keep in mind that antique jewelry is at least 100 years old, while vintage jewelry is 20 to 100 years old. This vintage and antique jewelry identification guide covers the major periods and the details you need to know.


---


## **Georgian Jewelry (1714–1830s)**


[Late Georgian Aquamarine and Gold Parure, ca. 1820](https://www.1stdibs.com/jewelry/earrings/drop-earrings/late-georgian-aquamarine-gold-parure/id-j_11199922/)


[Georgian jewelry](https://www.1stdibs.com/jewelry/style/georgian/) was handmade, often featuring closed-back settings, in which the gems have a thin layer of metallic foil behind them that reflects light and intensifies their color and brilliance. Jewelers sometimes overlaid a gold backing with silver, which enhances the white tone of diamonds but oxidizes as it ages, imparting a distinctive gray cast.


Among the jewelry styles that became popular during the Georgian era was archaeological revival, inspired by discoveries uncovered during excavations at Roman, Egyptian, Hellenistic and Etruscan sites. The designs are characterized by nature-inspired motifs and cannetille — filligree-like metalwork that added texture and detail.[Rundell, Bridge & Rundell](https://www.1stdibs.com/creators/rundell-bridge-and-rundell/) was one of the period’s notable jewelry houses.


---


## **Victorian Jewelry (1837–1901)**


[French Pearl, Ruby, Diamond and Gold Convertible Snake Bracelet/Necklace, ca. 1860](https://www.1stdibs.com/jewelry/necklaces/drop-necklaces/antique-french-pearl-ruby-diamond-gold-convertible-snake-bracelet-necklace-1860/id-j_1046382/)


The term[Victorian jewelry](https://www.1stdibs.com/jewelry/style/victorian/) encompasses pieces created during Queen Victoria’s 63-year reign. Unsurprisingly, the designs changed significantly over the course of this lengthy period.


Romantic-period (1837–60) jewelry, often feature exotic materials like seed pearls and turquoise. Pieces from the Grand or mourning period (1860–1880), influenced by the Queen Victoria’s grieving for her mother and her husband, Prince Albert, who both died in 1861, employ darker materials, like jet and onyx. Late Victorian or Aesthetic period (1880–1901) jewelry is more delicate, with a focus on nature themes.


[Garrard](https://www.1stdibs.com/creators/garrard/jewelry/) was a major jewelry house associated with Victorian design.


---


## **Art Nouveau Jewelry (1890–1910)**


[René Lalique Aquamarine Dragonfly Pendant, 1903–05](https://www.1stdibs.com/jewelry/necklaces/pendant-necklaces/rene-lalique-aquamarine-dragonfly-pendant/id-j_160198/)


The[Art Nouveau](https://www.1stdibs.com/jewelry/style/art-nouveau/) style debuted during the late Victorian period and continued until the start of World War I, in 1914. Art Nouveau jewelry, often modeled on natural subjects like flowers and insects, is characterized by flowing, asymmetrical designs that convey movement.


Enamel work became popular during the period, especially plique-à-jour, which allows light to pass through, similar to stained glass.[René Lalique](https://www.1stdibs.com/creators/rene-lalique/jewelry/) was the best-known jeweler of the era.


---


## **Edwardian Jewelry (1901–15)**


[Edwardian Old-Cut Cushion Diamond and Emerald Ring, 1900–09](https://www.1stdibs.com/jewelry/rings/engagement-rings/antique-edwardian-old-cut-cushion-diamond-20cts-emerald-ring-platinum/id-j_8809332/)


[Edwardian jewelry](https://www.1stdibs.com/jewelry/style/edwardian/) sported airy, intricate designs. Jewelers created the period’s characteristic “white on white” look by placing diamonds and light-colored stones in fine filigree and lacy platinum settings.


The period is associated with garland designs, featuring ribbons, bows and wreaths, and the millegrain technique, in which tiny metal beads create borders around stones and along the piece’s edges.[Cartier](https://www.1stdibs.com/creators/cartier/) was one of the defining jewelry houses of the Edwardian era.


---


## **Art Deco Jewelry (1920s–30s)**


[Cartier Platinum, Diamond and Sapphire Bracelet, 1930](https://www.1stdibs.com/jewelry/bracelets/link-bracelets/cartier-1930-art-deco-bracelet-platinum-2611-cwt-diamonds-sapphires/id-j_28894592/)


[Art Deco jewelry](https://www.1stdibs.com/jewelry/style/art-deco/) replaced the flowing forms of earlier periods with strong symmetry. Jewelers arranged diamonds and colorful gemstones in crisp geometric patterns, often using *calibré* -cut stones shaped to fit precisely into the design.


Cartier,[Van Cleef & Arpels](https://www.1stdibs.com/creators/van-cleef-and-arpels/) and[Boucheron](https://www.1stdibs.com/creators/boucheron/) were the major jewelry houses of the Art Deco era, developing the striking geometric style that makes the period’s pieces so recognizable.


---


## **Retro Jewelry (1930s–40s)**


[Gold, Ruby and Diamond Buckle Mesh Bracelet, 1945](https://www.1stdibs.com/jewelry/bracelets/retro-bracelets/high-jewellery-vintage-1945-18k-gold-ruby-diamond-buckle-mesh-bracelet/id-j_19900972/)


[Retro jewelry](https://www.1stdibs.com/jewelry/style/retro/) embraces color and big, bold forms and large, colorful gemstones. During World War II, platinum was restricted to military-related use, so jewelers worked more with gold, helping give the period’s pieces a distinctive look.


The French house Mauboussin, which debuted in 1827, is closely associated with the[Retro era’s](https://www.1stdibs.com/jewelry/style/retro/) oversize designs and dramatic cocktail jewelry.


---


## **Mid-Century Modern Jewelry (1945–60s)**


[Boucheron Paris Sapphire, Diamond, Gold and Platinum Tassel Necklace, 1950](https://www.1stdibs.com/jewelry/necklaces/multi-strand-necklaces/boucheron-paris-1950s-sapphire-diamond-18k-yellow-gold-platinum-tassel-necklace/id-j_28083962/)


**I**


Bold designs continued to characterize[mid-century jewelry](https://www.1stdibs.com/buy/mid-century-modern-jewelry/) , but they became more abstract and sculptural. Textured yellow gold was favored, along with sweeping curves and asymmetrical forms. The atomic age inspired designs referencing stars and modern technology.


Although gemstones were still used during the mid-century period to create visual impact, many jewelers made metalwork the focus.[Boucheron](https://www.1stdibs.com/creators/boucheron/jewelry/) , for example, created nature-inspired designs in platinum and gold, setting them with turquoise, lapis lazuli and malachite, all of which contributed to the era’s sophisticated character.


---


## **1970s & 1980s Vintage Jewelry**


[Grosse Modernist Yellow-Gold. Diamond and Lapis Necklace, 1971](https://www.1stdibs.com/jewelry/necklaces/link-necklaces/circa-1972-grosse-solid-18k-yellow-gold-modernist-diamond-lapis-necklace/id-j_27070362/)


Jewelry of the 1970s and 1980s is bold, making statements with chunky yellow-gold chains and textured finishes. Its oversize earrings and use of colorful gemstones represented a major change from previous periods.


[Bulgari](https://www.1stdibs.com/creators/bulgari/jewelry) was among the period’s defining jewelry house, a pioneer in producing large, colorful designs. Pieces from the[1970s](https://www.1stdibs.com/jewelry/period/1970s/) and[1980s](https://www.1stdibs.com/jewelry/period/1980s/) are very collectible today.


---


## **How to Identify Vintage Jewelry**


[Bulgari Monete Necklace with Ancient Silver Coins, 1980](https://www.1stdibs.com/jewelry/necklaces/link-necklaces/bulgari-ancient-silver-coin-monete-necklace/id-j_30658682/)


Style is your first clue to a piece’s age and origin, but construction details narrow down the possibilities. Closed-back settings, for example, are associated with earlier eras, while certain types of clasp can point to particular periods. Stone cuts provide yet another clue. Old-mine and old European cuts are common in antique and early vintage jewelry, whereas the round brilliant cut is seen in more-recent pieces.


[Hallmarks and maker’s marks](https://www.1stdibs.com/blogs/the-study/estate-jewelry/) identify metal purity and place of origin and sometimes even the individual jeweler. But they can fade with age and wear, so a difficult-to-read stamp isn’t a warning sign.


No single feature denotes a specific period, so consider the marks, construction, stones and overall style together. When making a purchase, take into account a piece’s rarity as well as its age and style.


---


## **Buy from a Vetted Seller**


You can’t contact the manufacturer of a vintage or antique jewel, so a seller you can trust is essential. Check a dealer’s reputation before you buy, and look for one who provides clear descriptions and condition details. Documentation is ideal, when available.


When you’re shopping for a significant purchase like an[antique engagement ring](https://www.1stdibs.com/info/antique-engagement-rings-buying-guide/) ,[vetted sellers](https://www.1stdibs.com/about/vetted-sellers/) can answer questions about provenance, materials, and previous repairs. And don’t forget the[1stDibs’ Promise](https://www.1stdibs.com/about/promise/) .

## **Frequently Asked Questions**


[Mario Buccellati 18-Karat Yellow-Gold, Turquoise and Pearl Dangle Earrings , 1970](https://www.1stdibs.com/jewelry/earrings/dangle-earrings/mario-buccellati-1970-dangle-earrings-18kt-yellow-gold-turquoises-pearls/id-j_22797042/)


### **What’s the difference between vintage and antique jewelry?**


Antique jewelry is at least 100 years old. Vintage jewelry is usually 20 to 100 years old.


### **How can I tell what era a piece of jewelry is from?**


Look for motifs, metals, gemstone cuts, settings, clasps and other details typical of a particular era. Hallmarks and maker’s marks are also clues.


### **What is the most valuable vintage-jewelry era?**


Value depends on rarity, condition, attribution and materials. The period of manufacture does not in itself determine value.


### **What’s the difference between Art Deco and Edwardian jewelry?**


Edwardian jewelry is typefied by delicate platinum filigree and intricate details. Art Deco designs are big and bold, displaying geometric symmetry.


### **How can I tell if a vintage piece is made with real gold and genuine gemstones?**


Check hallmarks, maker’s marks, construction and stone characteristics. If anything is unclear, ask for documentation. As always, buying from a vetted seller is your best bet.


### **Is it safe to buy vintage or antique jewelry online?**


Yes, but seller reputation matters. Vetted marketplaces, detailed listings, clear policies and authenticity guarantees reduce the risks of buying vintage jewelry online.


---
